content.content:
1	# Versioned updates — design
2	
3	Status: **agreed** (owner decisions recorded in §10; settled in the
4	2026-08-12 design conversation). Supersedes, once migrated, the unified
5	**baselining** task (`packs/basics/tasks/baselining/`) — its nightly
6	converge-everything-at-canon-head model, its date-held stamp, and its
7	four-condition agent escalation. The phased rollout is tracked as a
8	migration-plan issue (linked from the PR that lands this doc).
9	
10	Terminology decision (owner): the mechanism is called **update** — engine
11	update, pack update, install. The words *baseline / baselining /
12	rebaselining / rebasing* retire with the task that carried them.
13	
14	The shape: the canon splits into a **versioned engine** and **versioned
15	packs**, each with its own update flow. The engine update is fully
16	deterministic — no agentic stage, ever. The pack update keeps a bounded
17	agentic stage ("apply the new pack rules to this repo; repair what they
18	break") with one terminal escape hatch: any non-green end state leaves the
19	PR open, tagged `need-human`. Installing a pack is the same runner as
20	updating one, started from version zero.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 1. Why the current mechanism has an agentic stage at all
25	
26	The census (2026-08-12, this repo's full history — no migration record has
27	ever been deleted, so the population is complete): **three agentic notes
28	ever written**, across eleven migration records, plus three structural
29	escalation conditions in `worker.mjs`'s `escalation()`:
30	
31	| Residual | Cause | Lands in |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| `pack-independence` note | engine composition contract | member local packs |
34	| `prework-rename` note | engine field rename | member local packs |
35	| `fleet-baseline-task` note | pack lever conversion | member `.github/workflows/` |
36	| `withheld-workflows` | credential (Action token cannot write `.github/workflows/`) | — |
37	| `selftest-failed` / `checks-not-green` | judgment: is a non-green converge safe to merge? | — |
38	| executor-routine verification | the CCR routine is invisible to Actions | — |
39	
40	The lesson that shapes this design: the residuals split by **type**
41	(credential / judgment / member-content adaptation), not by which half of
42	the corpus changed. Two of the three notes were engine-caused but landed in
43	member-authored local packs the canon has never seen. So the split below
44	does not *eliminate* those types — it **relocates each to the one flow that
45	can absorb it**, and constrains the engine so its flow needs none of them.
46	
47	## 2. The engine: versioned, cloned, never agentic
48	
49	1. **The engine has running versions.** A release is a qualified snapshot
50	   (the live canary rehearsal runs against it once, per release, instead of
51	   the fleet discovering breakage per repo per night).
52	2. **The update procedure clones the engine release into the repo's mount**
53	   — wholesale replacement, as `compute-vendor-set` does today. The engine's
54	   own files never need migration; they are replaced.
55	3. **Engine migrations cover the member-owned files that reference engine
56	   surfaces** (hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, paths in local-pack code,
57	   the declaration file). They are **usually regex-replace rules, rarely
58	   code — never agentic** (owner decision). **The vendoring flow fetches
59	   only the migrations above the repo's installed engine version** (owner
60	   decision) — the version replaces today's date-based recency window
61	   (`recordDirIsRecent`) as the fetch predicate: an up-to-date repo
62	   vendors none, a lagging repo vendors exactly its gap. Because the same
63	   window currently also drives `migrationActive()` — the legacy-tolerance
64	   predicate consumer checks consult — that tolerance becomes
65	   version-based in the same move ("tolerate the legacy shape while
66	   installed version < N"), or checks would flag legacy shapes on repos
67	   that simply have not updated yet. The discipline this imposes on
68	   engine evolution is accepted and explicit: an engine contract change must
69	   either be mechanically expressible (regex or a small deterministic
70	   codemod shipped with the release) or remain backward-compatible, with the
71	   legacy shape accepted and normalized at load — the posture
72	   `prework-rename` already took. A contract change that satisfies neither
73	   **does not ship** until it does. There is no agentic lane to fall back
74	   on, by construction.
75	4. **The engine update does not write `.github/workflows/`.** The rare
76	   engine change that must touch a workflow file ships as a **custom
77	   update** — an explicitly named, separately credentialed operation (the
78	   Action token structurally cannot write there; the custom update runs
79	   under an MCP-credentialed session or a human). Naming it keeps the lane
80	   from becoming an invisible agentic side door.
81	5. **The engine update merges its PR to main automatically**, gated on the
82	   converged tree passing `selftest --strict` — the gate that exists because
83	   of #555, where an engine change silently stopped every consumer pack from
84	   validating while content checks stayed green. On a red self-test the PR
85	   stays open, tagged `need-human`. A **`force-merge-on-red-ci`** option
86	   (owner decision) overrides the gate for the operator who has judged the
87	   red acceptable — an explicit per-invocation flag, never a stored default.
88	
89	## 3. Packs: versioned, deterministic core, bounded agentic tail
90	
91	6. **Each pack has a version number**, and **each pack version declares the
92	   minimum engine version it requires**, enforced by the updater: a pack
93	   update never applies past the installed engine (§5). This is what makes
94	   the split coherent — the current single-snapshot guarantee ("the set and
95	   the content can never come from different snapshots") is replaced by a
96	   *checkable* compatibility constraint rather than dropped.
97	7. **A pack update is deterministic first**: vendor the new pack version,
98	   run its version-ranged migrations (vN→vN+1, in order), converge wiring.
99	   **Pack migrations live in the pack's own `migrations/` folder** and are
100	   fetched by the same version gate as the engine's (owner decision): only
101	   the records above the repo's installed version of *that pack* ship in
102	   the mount. The flat canon-wide `migrations/` directory does not survive
103	   the split — each record moves to the flow (engine or pack) that owns it.
104	   **Workflow churn belongs to the pack flow, explicitly** (owner decision):
105	   the scheduler workflow's content is a function of the *task set*
106	   (`declaredSecrets` unions `required_secrets` across discovered tasks), so
107	   pack changes are what rewrite it, and the pack flow carries the
108	   credential to land those files — the MCP lane baselining's agent stage
109	   uses today, §2b of its task.
110	8. **A pack update may carry an agentic stage**: "apply the new pack rules —
111	   fix the repo, repair the tests." This is the one place agentic work
112	   survives, because it is the one residual no mechanism can absorb: the
113	   pack's new rules meet member-authored content the canon has never seen.
114	   The stage also inherits the orphaned **executor-routine verification**
115	   (the CCR routine that fires on `ready-for-agent` is not a GitHub
116	   artifact; only an agent session can see it, and this is the only agent
117	   lane left).
118	
119	   **The word is *may*, and the RECORDS are what decide it** (#798). A pack
120	   record declares `applyStage: { why, instructions }`; an update whose gap
121	   holds no such record is delivered without a session. The first
122	   implementation asked the version plan instead — "any declared pack whose
123	   version moved" — and that is a fact about the *canon* where the stage
124	   needs a fact about the *member*. Because a record can only reach an
125	   up-to-date member if its pack's manifest bumps (§3.7), and every bump
126	   summoned a session, **a purely mechanical migration could not be shipped
127	   without spending an agent session on every member in the fleet**. The
128	   record's author knows which of the two kinds they wrote; a version number
129	   never can. An **install** stays unconditional (§4) — that genuinely is
130	   first contact.
131	9. **The pack update merges its PR to main** unless it ends non-green.
132	   **Every** non-green terminal — unanswered interview questions, an agentic
133	   repair that leaves checks red, a migration that could not complete —
134	   ends the same way: the PR stays open, the dispatch issue is tagged
135	   `need-human`, the run stops. Interviews are one instance of the rule,
136	   not the rule.
137	
138	## 4. Install = update from version zero
139	
140	Installing a pack is the pack updater started with no prior state: vendor,
141	converge, agentic apply, deliver — the same flow, same terminals (§3.9:
142	interview unanswered → PR open + `need-human`). **An install runs no
143	migrations** (owner decision): the vendored pack content is already the
144	newest shape, so there is no older state to migrate — replaying history
145	onto a fresh install is both wasted work and a correctness hazard
146	(migrations assume the shapes their era produced, not an empty repo).
147	The install stamps the pack's **latest** version directly; migrations are
148	exclusively for repos that were installed at an older one. Two
149	install-specific provisions:
150	
151	- **One-shot seed ops.** Some install effects are seeded once and owned by
152	  the repo thereafter (the README badge row is the existing precedent:
153	  seeded by `--badges` at adoption, never re-converged, precisely so
154	  updates cannot rewrite a member's README). The install carries an
155	  **initial migration** — ordinary code the runner executes, not a "real"
156	  migration — and the mechanism marks these ops *run-once-at-install*.
157	  The updater must never re-run them; the distinction between *seeded*
158	  (repo-owned from then on) and *converged* (rewritten every update)
159	  surfaces is load-bearing.
160	- The interview happens through the same open-PR + `need-human` terminal,
161	  which degrades gracefully to async — better than today's adopt-pack
162	  skill, which needs a live session.
163	
164	## 5. Invariants
165	
166	- **No agentic work in the engine flow.** Ever. The escape hatches are the
167	  named custom update (workflows) and the `need-human` terminal (red
168	  self-test) — both visible, neither a model.
169	- **Version-ranged migrations replace the date stamp.** "Which migrations
170	  apply" becomes "installed version → target version," retiring the
171	  held-stamp subtleties (#329, #330). The same range gates **fetching**:
172	  a mount carries exactly the migration records in its gap, none on an
173	  up-to-date repo, and a fresh install carries — and runs — none at all.
174	- **Compatibility is enforced, not assumed**: pack min-engine-version
175	  checked before apply; violation is a `need-human` terminal, not a guess.
176	- **Every non-green terminal looks the same**: PR open, `need-human`,
177	  stop. No flow merges red — except the engine's explicit
178	  `force-merge-on-red-ci`, which is an operator's signed judgment, not a
179	  flow default.
180	- **A repo that reports a clean update is clean.** The withholding pattern
181	  (paths silently dropped from a push, forever) does not survive: what a
182	  flow cannot write, it either hands to the flow that can (workflows → pack
183	  lane / custom update) or surfaces as `need-human`.
184	
185	  In practice this means the pack flow **stages** `.github/workflows/`
186	  content at `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` — a path its Action token
187	  *can* push — and ends at `apply-stage` until a session with an MCP
188	  credential moves it into place. Three properties, and the design needs all
189	  three: nothing is dropped (the update does not report clean while owing a
190	  file), the content is **reviewable** (it lands in the update's own PR diff,
191	  where a human sees the workflow change before any session touches it), and
192	  it is **recoverable** (a session that never ran leaves the content on the
193	  branch rather than losing it with a request file). The staging directory is
194	  swept every cycle, so it is empty exactly when nothing is owed — which is
195	  also what makes "did the apply stage actually run" a question with an
196	  answer (#797, #649).
197	
198	## 6. What this retires
199	
200	- The `baselining` task (task.md, task.mjs, worker.mjs), its escalation
201	  codes, and its dispatch-issue protocol.
202	- The `agentic:` field on migration records: engine migrations may not
203	  carry it at all; pack migrations express agentic work as the pack
204	  update's apply stage instead, by declaring `applyStage: { why,
205	  instructions }` (§3.8). What the successor drops is the **model** knob —
206	  which model runs a session is the scheduler's answer, off the task
207	  declaration, and a record naming its own was a second authority over the
208	  same fact.
209	- The date-held stamp (`claudinite.updated` gating note application).
210	- The baselining vocabulary, corpus-wide.
211	
212	## 7. Known-open
213	
214	- The `local-pack-namespace` declaration rewrite (bare id → `local/<id>`)
215	  remains unowned; the versioned scheme should place it in an engine
216	  migration (it is a regex on the declaration file — squarely within §2.3).
217	- Escalation-frequency measurement across the fleet (which `escalation()`
218	  codes actually fire) would validate the split's cost model; nice to have
219	  before Phase 2, not a blocker.
220	
221	## 8. Propagation and session access
222	
223	**Member repos change nothing by hand, and their local packs change not at
224	all.** Local packs are repo-owned, not distributed: under this scheme they
225	get no version numbers, no `migrations/` folders, and no install flow, and
226	the cutover never rewrites them. The one indirect touch is
227	`migrationActive()` tolerance moving from date-based to version-based —
228	shipped together with the fetch gate (§2.3) so a lagging repo's local
229	packs keep their legacy-shape tolerance until that repo actually updates.
230	A local pack's adaptation remains what it is today: a conformance finding
231	resolved in the repo's own sessions, never a step of this migration.
232	
233	The member-side deltas the migration does produce are all written by the
234	flows themselves: new stamp fields in `.claudinite-checks.json`
235	(installed engine version, per-pack versions, the which-mechanism rollout
236	flag), the relocated migration records inside the vendored mount, and
237	eventually the new worker.
238	
239	**Implementation happens in the canon repo alone** — no fleet-scoped
240	session is required. The propagation channel already exists and is
241	self-carrying: the vendored worker shallow-clones fresh canon every cycle
242	and executes the *cloned* canon's vendoring, wiring, and migration
243	scripts as subprocesses, never its own stale copies (worker.mjs:14–25,
244	51–54). New vendor-set logic, the per-pack migration layout, and the
245	version gate are live fleet-wide the night after they land in canon;
246	changes to the worker/driver itself lag exactly one cycle (vendored in
247	cycle N, executing in N+1). Three caveats, none requiring fleet access to
248	implement:
249	
250	1. **Scheduler workflow stub changes** land per-repo through the existing
251	   agent lane (baselining §2b's MCP credential; the pack flow's lane after
252	   Phase 2) — automatic, during each repo's own cycle.
253	2. **The CCR executor routines** are the one per-repo artifact outside
254	   GitHub's reach. Their prompt is a thin pointer to the vendored
255	   `executor.md`, so content changes ride the mount; only a change to the
256	   dispatch *wiring* (label name, model, launcher prompt) would need
257	   per-repo trigger-API access. The rollout should avoid requiring that —
258	   or accept the bootstrap-Part-6 owner-issue path where it cannot.
259	3. **The fleet-wide cutover verification** (Phase 5's precondition) is
260	   fleet-scoped, but it belongs to the sheepdog enforcer's existing fleet
261	   tasks — machinery, not an implementation session.
262	
263	## 9. Migration
264	
265	Phased rollout tracked in the migration-plan issue (filed alongside this
266	doc). Summary: version scaffolding first (no behavior change), then the
267	engine flow, then the pack flow, then install, then retirement of
268	baselining and its vocabulary.
269	
270	## 10. Owner decisions recorded
271	
272	1. Engine auto-merge is selftest-gated, **with a `force-merge-on-red-ci`
273	   override** (2026-08-12).
274	2. Workflow churn is **explicitly the pack flow's** (2026-08-12).
275	3. Engine migrations are "usually regex, rarely code" — **no agentic work
276	   on the engine, ever** (2026-08-12).
277	4. `need-human` covers **all** non-green terminals, not only interviews
278	   (2026-08-12).
279	5. Pack versions **declare and enforce** a minimum engine version
280	   (2026-08-12).
281	6. The mechanism is named **update**; baselining vocabulary retires
282	   (2026-08-12).
283	7. Migration fetching is **version-gated**: vendoring ships only the
284	   records above the repo's installed version — engine and pack alike —
285	   replacing the date-based recency window (2026-08-12).
286	8. Pack migrations live in **each pack's own `migrations/` folder**; the
287	   flat canon-wide directory retires with the split (2026-08-12).
288	9. **An install runs no migrations**: the vendored content is already the
289	   newest shape, and the install stamps the latest version directly
290	   (2026-08-12).

1	# Adopting Claudinite
2	
3	How a consuming repo adopts these shared guidelines, under the **vendored mount**
4	([vendoring/DESIGN.md](vendoring/DESIGN.md)): adoption is the **one network moment** — fetch the canon
5	once, vendor what this repo needs into **tracked files** under `.claudinite/shared/`, wire the
6	hooks — and every session after runs **offline** from the committed snapshot. The nightly
7	maintenance is the only regular updater. Idempotent: re-running refreshes the snapshot exactly
8	like a nightly would (fetch → converge → stamp) and never clobbers your own config — your own
9	`settings.json` entries are only ever added to, never overwritten.
10	
11	## Part 1 — fetch the canon (the network moment)
12	
13	```sh
14	scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
15	curl -fsSL https://codeload.github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tar.gz/main \
16	  | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C "$scratch"
17	ref="$(git ls-remote https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite.git main 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
18	```
19	
20	Adoption (and an on-demand refresh) is the only time a consumer fetches — sessions never do, so
21	the environment's network policy no longer needs `codeload.github.com` for day-to-day work.
22	
23	## Part 2 — write the pack declaration (and run the adoption interview)
24	
25	```sh
26	node "$scratch/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs" --init
27	```
28	
29	`--init` seeds `.claudinite-checks.json`: the baseline, the technology packs the repo's
30	fingerprint suspects, the default-on maintenance packs, each declared pack's `requires` closure,
31	and `"maintenance": { "delivery": "auto-merge" }`. A fingerprint only *suspects* a pack — from here on
32	the declaration is authoritative and adding/dropping packs is the project's call. Offer the owner
33	that call from the full pack directory (`$scratch/packs/directory.GENERATED.md` — id, coverage,
34	activation and requires for every adoptable pack; it also vendors into the mount, so later
35	sessions re-read it from `.claudinite/shared/`). Settings
36	**validity** is enforced at load: an unknown pack name, an unknown property, or malformed JSON is
37	a blocking `config` error.
38	
39	If `--init` prints **pending adoption questions**, run the adoption interview now — this is the
40	one strict point (the owner is present by construction; outside bootstrap the same gap only ever
41	surfaces as a mild SessionStart note — [packs/README.md](packs/README.md#adoption-interview-questions)):
42	ask the owner each question via `AskUserQuestion`, record each answer **verbatim** on that pack's
43	entry as `answers: { "<question-id>": "<answer>" }` ("n/a — none wanted" is a valid answer), and
44	derive the entry's `config` where the question's distill note says how.
45	
46	## Part 3 — vendor the snapshot
47	
48	```sh
49	node "$scratch/vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs" --target . ${ref:+--ref "$ref"}
50	```
51	
52	This materializes the repo's vendor set — the engine, the mount, the declared packs with their
53	skills, the full pack directory — under `.claudinite/shared/` at canon-relative paths, and stamps the
54	declaration (`"claudinite": { "updated": "YYYY-MM-DD", "ref": "<sha>" }`). Whole-set convergence:
55	re-running it (or declaring a new pack and re-running) rebuilds the tree; errors abort before any
56	write. The `shared/` root is a **submodule emulation** — a future `git submodule add … .claudinite/shared`
57	lands a superset at the same path with no wiring change (see the design doc).
58	
59	## Part 4 — track it
60	
61	```sh
62	for rule in '/.claudinite-hooks.log' '/.claudinite-hooks.log.tmp'; do
63	  grep -qxF "$rule" .gitignore 2>/dev/null || echo "$rule" >> .gitignore
64	done
65	git add .gitignore .claudinite-checks.json .claudinite/shared
66	```
67	
68	That is the **whole** ignore contract: the two hook-log lines. The vendored world writes
69	nothing untracked into `.claudinite/` — `shared/` and `local_packs/` are ordinary tracked
70	trees — so nothing there needs ignoring (#385).
71	
72	## Part 5 — wire the hooks
73	
74	Claude Code runs `SessionStart` entries **in parallel, in non-deterministic order**, so anything
75	sequenced must live inside **one** entry. Register exactly one — the orchestrator, which runs
76	the context steps in sequence in a single process (self-test → active-pack prose → each
77	active pack's own session-start step → skill mounts → env check → interview check) and forwards their stdout into the session context:
78	
79	```json
80	{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [
81	  { "type": "command", "command": "bash $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/session-start-command.sh" }
82	] } ] } }
83	```
84	
85	Register the Stop hook (runs the **work-scope** checks when the session changed something —
86	judging the change in front of the session, with the transcript — and blocks the stop while
87	blocking findings remain), the PreToolUse guard (deterministically blocks forbidden commands),
88	and the SessionEnd runner (invokes each active pack's own `session-end.mjs`, once, when the
89	session ends — best-effort and fail-soft: it can never block a session from ending, and nothing
90	depends on it having run) alongside it. The **world-scope** sweep is not wired here — it goes
91	into the project's test/CI flow in Part 8:
92	
93	```json
94	{ "hooks": { "Stop": [ { "hooks": [
95	  { "type": "command", "command": "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/stop-command.mjs" }
96	] } ],
97	  "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [
98	  { "type": "command", "command": "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/pretooluse-command.mjs" }
99	] } ],
100	  "SessionEnd": [ { "hooks": [
101	  { "type": "command", "command": "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs" }
102	] } ] } }
103	```
104	
105	Invoke scripts **through `bash`/`node`**, never as bare paths — a dropped exec bit would fail the
106	hook before line 1 and swallow its own message. Notes on how the steps behave:
107	
108	- **A pack may contribute its own session-start step** — the orchestrator runs
109	  `<pack>/session-start.mjs` for every declared pack that ships one, hands it that pack's
110	  entry `config`, and forwards what it prints into the session context under the pack's
111	  marker. It is for what a pack can only know at session time (content from outside this
112	  repo, or keyed to the person in front of it), where `RULES.md` is fixed at vendor time.
113	  Bounded and **fail-soft**: a step that fails, hangs, or overruns the context cap is one
114	  plain-text note and the session proceeds. Which packs contribute one is the packs'
115	  business, not bootstrap's.
116	- **The session opens by stating what loaded** — a last step counts the active packs, their
117	  checks, the token weight of the prose injected and the skills mounted, and emits that as one
118	  line the session repeats back before anything else. A pack whose step computed something worth
119	  adding to it says so on the facet channel (a `CLAUDINITE-FACET:` line), which the orchestrator
120	  opens and cleans up; core learns no pack's name to carry a facet.
121	- **The halt-gate** — a SessionStart hook cannot block, but its stdout is injected into context,
122	  so a step that can't do its load-bearing job (`env.mjs check` — a missing toolchain) prints a
123	  plain-text directive telling the assistant to STOP and confirm via `AskUserQuestion` before any
124	  work. Plain text always — one hook's stdout must never mix JSON and prose.
125	- **The durable hook log** — every hook appends `start` / `done exit=N` lines to
126	  `.claudinite-hooks.log` at the repo root. No lines ⇒ the hook never triggered; `start` without
127	  `done` ⇒ it died executing. Reach for it first when a session says the harness didn't load.
128	- **Skill mounts are session-generated, never committed** — `shared/engine/skill_loader/mount-skills.mjs`
129	  (an orchestrator step) regenerates `.claude/skills/<name>` symlinks for the declared packs'
130	  union each session and maintains a self-ignoring `.gitignore` there; a committed link would
131	  dangle on every plain checkout.
132	
133	One standing rule the vendored tree does **not** change: committed consumer code must not
134	`import`/`require` canon helpers from `.claudinite/` — the canon is refreshed nightly and
135	refactored upstream, so code reaching into it inherits every rename as a breaking change. Inline
136	what you need. The `claudinite-isolation` check enforces this outside the wiring files.
137	
138	## Part 6 — schedule the repo (it schedules itself)
139	
140	A consuming project schedules **itself** (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §9). As part of
141	adoption:
142	
143	1. **Vendor the scheduler workflow** — copy `claudinite-scheduler.yml` into
144	   `.github/workflows/` and rewrite its placeholder cron minute to this repo's stable
145	   hashed minute in :10–:50 (the repo's only cron). Compute the minute — never guess it —
146	   with the vendored hasher: `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs
147	   <owner/repo>`. It is a pure function of the repo full name, so it is the same value on
148	   every re-vendor and the update task re-derives it to catch drift. This step, the Part 5
149	   hook registrations, dropping the retired `@.claudinite/shared/CLAUDE.md` import, the
150	   rules index (`.claudinite/claudinite-rules.GENERATED.md` and its `CLAUDE.md` import), this
151	   repo's own seed local pack, and the README pack-badge row (below)
152	   are all mechanized by `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs
153	   <owner/repo> --badges --seed-local-pack` — the single wiring surface bootstrap and the update
154	   flows both call, so the set is defined once in code, not re-enacted from this prose each
155	   night. Pass both flags here and only here: they are the surfaces adoption seeds that the
156	   nightly deliberately does not (step 2).
157	2. **The README pack-badge row needs no step either** — the same converge writes a
158	   one-line row of the declared packs' badges into `README.md`, under the title, between
159	   `<!-- claudinite:packs -->` markers — the opening one on its own line above the badges,
160	   so the badges are not swallowed by the HTML block a line beginning with `<!--` opens;
161	   anything the repo writes after the closing marker
162	   on that line is its own and is never touched. **This is a one-time seed.** Baselining
163	   runs the same converge WITHOUT `--badges`, so from here the row is the repo's own text
164	   — edit it, move it, or delete it, and nothing will argue. A README belongs to its repo,
165	   and a nightly-derived row would put a README diff in the update commit every time
166	   the declaration moved.
167	3. **Labels need no step** — the tick and the executor ensure the queue's labels
168	   (`task:blocked`, `task:ready`, `task:urgent`, `task:executing`, `task:agent`,
169	   `origin:schedule`, `needs-human`, the `outcome:*` set) exist before applying any
170	   of them (create-if-missing, idempotent), so they materialize on the first run and
171	   self-heal if deleted. No one-off creation, nothing to forget.
172	4. **Write the `taskScheduler` key** into `.claudinite-checks.json` (defaults:
173	   `{ "dailyHour": 4, "weeklyDay": "Sun", "monthlyDay": 1 }`, all UTC) — the repo's
174	   own anchors, from which the tick decides when each task's item comes due.
175	5. **Create the executor routine and wire it as an invocation endpoint.** The
176	   executor starts an agent session with an **API call**, not a label event, so this
177	   is two halves that only work together — and a repo with one half has a queue that
178	   fills and never hands anything off.
179	
180	   a. **Create the routine** via the trigger API, named `Claudinite executor - <repo>`,
181	      whose whole stored prompt is the one line
182	      `Execute the Claudinite work item: .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md`.
183	      Everything a task session does comes from that tracked file; a prompt carrying
184	      instructions of its own is behavior nobody reviews. Sources = **this repo alone**
185	      (not the Claudinite canon — the update runner fetches canon Action-side, so no
186	      task needs it in session).
187	
188	   b. **Point the repo at it.** Take the routine's API trigger URL and add it to
189	      `.claudinite-checks.json` under the key every task uses unless it names another:
190	
191	      ```json
192	      "taskScheduler": { "endpoints": { "default": {
193	        "url": "[REDACTED:env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL]/v1/claude_code/routines/<trigger-id>/fire",
194	        "tokenSecret": "CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN"
195	      } } }
196	      ```
197	
198	      `tokenSecret` is the **name** of a repo Actions secret, never a token — the
199	      config is tracked, so nothing adjacent to a credential goes in it. Set that
200	      secret to the routine's bearer token.
201	
202	   The API sets only name, prompt and environment; **the repo binding and the model
203	   are UI-only**, so every routine an agent creates arrives unfinished. Do not file a
204	   separate issue for the remainder — a config that lives away from the thing it
205	   configures is a config someone reads once and never reconciles. **Carry the
206	   leftover steps in the routine's own prompt**, as a block below the launcher line
207	   whose last instruction is to delete itself:
208	
209	   > `--- SETUP — delete this block once done, leaving only the line above ---`
210	   > 1. Model → Sonnet 5.
211	   > 2. Repo → `<owner>/<repo>`, and that repo alone (source and outcome).
212	
213	   The routine then states its own unfinished-ness where the owner is already looking to
214	   fix it, and finishing it and clearing the block are the same edit — so a
215	   half-configured executor cannot quietly pass for a working one.
216	
217	   Neither half fails silently if it is missing: the hand-off names exactly what is
218	   unset — the endpoint, its `url`, its `tokenSecret`, or the secret itself — on the
219	   work item, and converges that item to `needs-human`. Agentless tasks keep working
220	   throughout, since they never reach this path.
221	
222	## Part 7 — categorize the project (declare its class pack)
223	
224	**Only for a fresh / empty project** — one without its own established working style. The owner
225	runs recurring **classes** of project, each carried by a project-class pack:
226	
227	1. Ask the owner which class this project is, offering the project-class packs under
228	   [`packs/`](packs/) as the options.
229	2. A class pack fits → add its id to `"packs"` in `.claudinite-checks.json` and re-run Part 3
230	   (a declaration change triggers a whole-set refresh, so the new pack's content lands).
231	3. No class pack fits → run the project-instructions skill: it decomposes the project into pack
232	   facets and extracts its working instructions into new/refined canon packs (the primary
233	   deliverable) plus a thin project-specific overlay.
234	
235	## Part 8 — wire both sweeps into the test/CI flow, and land green
236	
237	Two commands, answering two different questions. Wire each in as its own step, invoked as the
238	standalone command (both are the engine's always-vendored Node CLIs, so they run in any flow
239	regardless of the project's own language — **never** add either as a language-specific test file
240	a runner discovers):
241	
242	```sh
243	node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs                    # the TREE
244	node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs --branch "$BRANCH"   # the CHANGE
245	```
246	
247	The **world** sweep is a whole-repo invariant assertion — the same shape as a test suite. The
248	**work** sweep judges this branch's diff against the base branch, which is the only way to see
249	what a change *did* rather than what the repo now contains: whether a commit references its
250	issue, whether a merge commit slipped in, whether an edit that must carry something with it did.
251	The Stop hook runs the work scope too, but only where a session runs — an unattended commit or a
252	hand-pushed branch reaches `main` unjudged otherwise.
253	
254	`ci-work-scope.mjs` owns everything that makes that sweep meaningful, so a project carries the
255	invocation and never the recipe: it fetches the base branch (a CI checkout has none, and a
256	baseless scope is an empty diff that passes every rule), refuses a scope that would judge
257	nothing, skips the engine's own `claudinite/…` branches (their PRs have no issue behind them,
258	and their auto-merge is a queue for checks — a red check there stops the repo updating rather
259	than annoying anyone), and exits non-zero on a blocking finding. Pass `--branch` wherever the
260	checkout is detached (GitHub Actions: `${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}`), since a
261	detached head reports no branch name and the skip above would never fire.
262	
263	- **The project already has a test/CI flow** (a CI job, a `make test` target, an npm/pnpm
264	  `test` script, a `justfile`, …): add both commands as two more steps, so a red sweep fails that
265	  flow exactly like a failing test.
266	- **The project has none:** add a **minimal** flow — a single CI job (or a `make`/script target)
267	  whose steps run the project's own tests, if any, then the two commands above. The point is a
268	  deterministic place both sweeps run at each change; keep it as small as the repo needs.
269	- **The work sweep needs the base branch reachable**, so a CI checkout must not be shallow to the
270	  point of hiding it (`fetch-depth: 0` on `actions/checkout`); the entry point fetches the ref
271	  itself and fails loudly rather than judging an empty diff.
272	
273	Then run the world sweep once locally and clear what it surfaces. On a repo with existing code,
274	**expect a backlog** — enforcement scope is whole-repo, and findings in code you never touched
275	would otherwise fail every future run. Fix causes, or record a reasoned `accept` in
276	`.claudinite-checks.json` for the deliberate keeps. Don't reach for `--changed` to hide the
277	backlog — it is a transitional aid, never the enforcement default. Commit the adoption as one
278	change (the vendored tree, the declaration, the hook wiring, the test/CI step) and push it
279	through the normal PR flow.
280	
281	## Part 9 — cloud environment setup (Claude Code on the web)
282	
283	The web base image ships no toolchains; installs belong in the environment **image** (built
284	once, snapshotted), not a per-session hook. The script to paste is a pack's, not core's —
285	[`packs/README.md`](packs/README.md#environment-requirements) names it and the pack that owns it.
286	Its body is identical for every project: paste it whole into the environment's **Setup script**
287	field and rebuild (`find .claudinite/shared -name environment-setup-command.sh` locates it in a
288	mount). It runs each active pack's declared installs
289	(`env.mjs install`, driven by the declaration); the SessionStart `env.mjs check` then only
290	*probes* and halt-gates on a genuinely missing prerequisite. The network policy must reach what
291	the active packs install from (npm registry, `pub.dev`, …) — the corpus itself is already in the
292	checkout.
293	
294	## Bespoke merge policy (optional)
295	
296	The portable merge recipe ships as the merge skill and needs nothing from you (squash via PR,
297	gate on CI only when the repo has it). Only if your project genuinely diverges: put the policy in
298	its own file and **name it explicitly in your `CLAUDE.md`** — the recipe reads it only then.

Record action="needs-decision".
   c. **Blocked by another still-open issue** (the issue itself says so, or clearly depends on one) — label "blocked" and comment `blocked by #N`, ending with `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=blocked -->`. Record action="blocked".
   d. **Small and quick to do** (a well-scoped, clearly small task, not yet done) — label "quick-win" and comment scoping it briefly, ending with `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=quick-win -->`. Record action="quick-win".
   e. **Else** — take no action. Record action="left".

Important safeguards:
- Never close an issue you cannot cite specific main-content evidence for.
- Never re-post a comment whose verdict matches the immediately-prior claudinite:tidy-issues marker comment (step 3 above) — that must resolve to "unchanged" with NO github write at all.
- Only ever comment/label/close — never touch PRs, branches, or push code.
- Be conservative: when genuinely unsure, choose "left" (no action) rather than guessing.

After processing all 5 issues, report back ONLY a structured summary, one line per issue, in this exact format:
#<n>: action=<closed|needs-decision|blocked|quick-win|left|unchanged> note="<one-line note, e.g. what you closed with/cited, or prior verdict+date for unchanged>"

Keep your final report terse — just the 5 lines plus nothing else.

    Retire the slot scheduler: delete run.mjs, the slot half of slots.mjs, the slot stub and FORCE_TASKS (#993)
    
    * Retire the slot scheduler's code, keeping the four things the queue still needs
    
    run.mjs, the slot half of slots.mjs, the slot workflow stub and the run
    ledger's watermark go. Extraction rides with the deletion rather than
    preceding it, so nothing is duplicated against a still-live run.mjs:
    
    - slots.mjs -> calendar.mjs: the frequency vocabulary and the anchor
      arithmetic, with no occurrence identity in it. queue/anchors.mjs
      delegates; task-contract and task-declaration-shape read the vocabulary.
    - buildSignalContext -> signals/context.mjs.
    - ensureLabels: task-janitor imports it from github.mjs, its real home.
    - runPrecondition -> evaluatePrecondition on the queue's executor, which
      is now the only place a precondition is called.
    
    The run ledger's writer half (renderTaskRun(s), taskRunOutcome) goes with
    it; the parser stays, since Actions logs the slot scheduler wrote are
    still inside retention and the usage fold reads them.
    
    taskScheduler.dispatch loses its "slots" value rather than silently
    meaning the queue: a parameter that stops being read must fail loudly.
    
    Refs #974
    
    * Guard the prework environment against a parameter channel nobody sets
    
    A task reading a CLAUDINITE_* variable prework never hands it fails in the
    one way nothing catches: process.env.X is undefined, the parse yields an
    empty result, and the run goes green having done something else. That is
    how three fleet tasks kept taking parameters through CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES
    after the queue stopped setting it — REPOS could not bound the sweep and
    DRY_RUN could not withhold its writes, so every fleet-baseline run was
    unscoped and live.
    
    The legal set is the key set of the object the executor actually builds
    (preworkEnv, now the single place those names are written), imported rather
    than restated, so the guard quantifies over the contract instead of naming
    the variables that were broken this time.
    
    The update worker's CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF is accepted here with its reason:
    the canary rehearsal workflow is a second, deliberate caller that sets it.
    
    Refs #974
    
    * Move the four parameterized tasks onto the item's Context
    
    fleet-baseline, fleet-add-missing-packs, fleet-digest and
    adopt-requested-packs took their operator parameters through
    CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES, which the queue never sets. They read
    CLAUDINITE_CONTEXT now, parsed by one pack-local bag in
    packs/sheepdog/param-bag.mjs.
    
    Two things the change turns on:
    
    - The executor passes the ITEM's own Context to prework, unioned with the
      precondition's, and writes the union back at hand-off. Only the verdict's
      half reached prework before, so a hand-created item's --context lines were
      unreachable by the worker they were typed for.
    - The bag takes only SHOUTING KEY[=value] tokens. Context is binding scope

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [x] The first member flipped, wired and observed end to end — agentless and agentic
- [ ] All members flipped and observed; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] Step 4: the fielded engine matches DESIGN §15.14–24 — #883 closed
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

{"number":972,"title":"core/scheduled-tasks.md teaches a stale task model — agentic-only, cron-defined","body":"## The problem

`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md` is the doc every session reads before writing or changing a task (`core/RULES.md`). It still describes the **slot** mechanism, which is now the legacy opt-out — `dispatchMode` in `engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs` defaults to `queue`. Two wrong models come out of it, both confirmed against a live session:

**1. "A task is agentic work."** The doc opens with a scheduler that "creates dispatch issues (`ready-for-agent`) for agentic work", and treats `agent_model: none` as a footnote exception. The engine says the opposite: `engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs` runs prework in the drain job and, when no agent is requested, **closes the item right there** — `Prework did this run's work; no agent was needed.` A task is deterministic code by default with an *optional* agentic phase. A task that runs a script in GitHub Actions with no dedicated workflow file is the ordinary shape, not a special case.

**2. "A task is a scheduled run."** The title says "Scheduled tasks"; the framing hangs every task off the hourly cron. Under the queue, the cron only drives the tick's *instantiation* of recurring items. Items are equally created by hand (`create-work-item`), by other tasks, by fan-out, and by a `wake` dispatch input; `manual` tasks are never instantiated by the tick at all (DESIGN §8). Scheduling is one origin among several.

The "the repo's **only** cron" sentence lands in the middle of this and gets read as the *definition* of a task rather than as what it is — a property of the scheduler workflow.

## Also stale in the same doc

- The three-responsibility split (scheduler / executor / janitor) — the queue refines this to four roles, and the scheduler's half that evaluated preconditions has moved into the executor.
- "re-arming lost trigger events" as a janitor job — the post-tick drain retires the re-arm.
- The executor described as "a per-repo routine fired by the label event" — it is a pull worker, and the drain is what keeps common-case latency at zero.

## The ask

Rewrite the doc around the current model, keep the one-cron invariant where it belongs (a scheduler-workflow property, still enforced by `engine/selftest.mjs`), and sweep the references. Historical design records under `docs/` are a record of their moment — links only, no content rewrites.

1	# Scheduled tasks — the per-project scheduling mechanism
2	
3	How a repo's recurring Claudinite work runs. A repo schedules **itself**, and
4	every occurrence of every task is an **issue in that repo** — a `[claudinite-work]`
5	work item whose labels are its state. That is the work-item queue; what follows is
6	the contract a task is written to, not how the queue works internally.
7	
8	Three responsibilities, strictly separated (owner, 2026-08-06):
9	
10	1. **The tick** — a vendored hourly Action
11	   (`.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`) that is pure label mechanics
12	   over the issue list: **instantiate** each recurring task's standing item when
13	   its anchor comes, **ready** blocked items whose wait has passed, **reclaim**
14	   dead executor claims. It evaluates no precondition and collects no signal.
15	2. **The executor** — a pull worker over the queue (the tick's post-tick drain,
16	   and a `labeled`-event run for latency) that picks the next ready item, claims
17	   it, evaluates **that one task's** precondition, runs its prework, and either
18	   converges the item or hands off to an agent session.
19	3. **The task-janitor** — an ordinary daily task (`basics/task-janitor`,
20	   `agent_model: none`) that owns everything about the queue that is *nobody's
21	   task*: items stuck ready past their period, items wearing no state label after
22	   a torn transition, and a health review of the open set.
23	
24	The engine is vendored under `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/`; the basics
25	pack owns the conformance guards for the surfaces a repo authors around it —
26	scheduling is baseline Claudinite discipline, present wherever basics is
27	declared (everywhere), not an opt-in feature.
28	
29	There is no watermark and no per-run state: an occurrence exists because its
30	issue exists, which is why an outage self-heals by looking at the queue rather
31	than by replaying a ledger.
32	
33	## What the checks guard
34	
35	- **The scheduler workflow is a thin shim.** The vendored
36	  `claudinite-scheduler.yml` carries a single **hourly** cron on a repo-hashed
37	  minute constrained to **:10–:50** (the one repo-specific value in the stub —
38	  `engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs`, a pure function of the repo full name that
39	  bootstrap stamps in and baselining re-derives), a `concurrency` group, a
40	  `workflow_dispatch` trigger (whose one `wake` input is how a task is forced,

tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/**/*.test.mjs)
          # Deliberately oversubscribed. node --test defaults to one worker per core

1	# Making changes to Claudinite without hurting consumers
2	
3	> **Status: provisional — beliefs, not law.** Every entry here says what we're *currently* doing
4	> and *why we think* it helps. When an entry blocks a better change, challenge the entry rather
5	> than contorting the change; being cited in this guide is not, by itself, a reason something
6	> must stay. We'll solidify entries once they've earned it.
7	
8	Claudinite is vendored into every consuming repo, so a change here lands in many places, on the
9	fleet's schedule, usually with no human watching. This guide collects what we currently believe
10	about making such changes safely. It is a maintainer document for sessions working *in* this
11	repo; it is not part of the vendored corpus.
12	
13	## First, know which channel the change travels
14	
15	Since the fleet moved to the tracked vendored mount (vendoring/DESIGN.md, phases 1–3 complete),
16	the channel model is small — nothing reaches a consumer instantly, and nothing arrives outside
17	its git history:
18	
19	- **The vendored corpus** (`engine/`, `packs/` — checks, prose, bundled skills) — each member
20	  holds a tracked snapshot under `.claudinite/shared/`, converged **whole-set** to the canon
21	  head by the nightly refresh and stamped with its provenance. Propagation lags one nightly,
22	  lands as a reviewable commit on the member's `claudinite/maintenance` PR (auto-merged on
23	  `auto-merge` delivery once the repo's checks pass, held for the owner on `review`), and the
24	  rollback story is the same channel: fix the canon, the next nightly re-heals. A wrong
25	  *blocking* check still fails every member's Stop hook — visible and recoverable, but
26	  fleet-wide noise, so treat check changes as production changes.
27	- **Migration notes** (`engine/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`, or `packs/<pack>/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`) — the channel for anything convergence
28	  can't express: renames of consumer-held wiring, declaration rewrites, one-off agentic steps.
29	  Stamp-day-gated and idempotent; the note's `legacyPresent` telemetry says when the fleet has
30	  moved and (for `retire: 'auto'`) retires the record itself.
31	- **Copied artifacts** (pack `stubs/`, seeded configs) — these do **not** propagate at all. Each
32	  consumer holds its own copy, which drifts silently unless a check enforces its shape. Changing
33	  the source file alone only affects repos bootstrapped *after* the change.
34	- **Bootstrap wiring** (the committed artifacts [bootstrap.md](bootstrap.md) seeds:
35	  `settings.json` hook registrations, the two gitignore lines, the pack declaration) —
36	  propagates through the nightly update's idempotent backfills on the same delivery PR.
37	  The discipline: a change here is written as steps that **converge from every layout in the
38	  wild**, not just from the latest.
39	
40	Out-of-repo state remains the one channel git never reaches: a web environment's pasted Setup
41	script is snapshotted at environment build. A change that moves what the pasted script calls
42	needs the script's own probe to fail fast and a member issue asking for the one human action
43	(re-paste).
44	
45	## Migrating a copied artifact (stubs and the like)
46	
47	Because copies won't move on their own, we currently migrate them through the conformance
48	checks, in one Claudinite-only change:
49	
50	1. Change the source artifact in the pack (the stub under `packs/<pack>/stubs/`).
51	2. Make sure the pack's conformance check enforces the properties that changed, with a `fix`
52	   that says how to align (usually "re-copy the stub"). A consumer's own next session then
53	   raises a blocking finding and performs the migration in that repo — no per-repo PR from
54	   here.
55	3. Keep the pack's `detect` fingerprint **tolerant of the legacy shape** while copies migrate
56	   (e.g. a `LEGACY_*` list beside the current constant), so a fresh `--init` still recognizes a
57	   not-yet-migrated repo and seeds the pack.
58	
59	Fleet-wide "everyone has migrated" telemetry exists — declare the rename as a
60	[baseline migration](engine/migrations/README.md), **in the same change that introduces the tolerance**: a
61	tolerance that lands without its record has no signal that will ever retire it. Any legacy shape a
62	tolerance keeps readable (an old path, a stub's old form, a legacy key *inside* a consumer's config
63	file) is trackable the same way, `legacyPresent` reading whatever expresses the old shape. The
64	fleet census probes every repo for the legacy shape and **auto-retires** the migration once none
65	remain. While a migration's tolerance still lives inline (readers not yet consulting its
66	`resolvePath`), keep it `retire:'manual'` and drop it deliberately.
67

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor

- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887

- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. {"number":950,"title":"A parked update PR is not a successful converge — exit non-zero","body":"Refs #939. This is the half of #939 that made it *invisible*, and it's separable from the delivery-semantics decision that issue still needs.

## The defect

When the update flow's terminal is `needs-human`, the converge has **delivered nothing** — the PR is open, parked, waiting for a person. But the runner labelled the PR and then **returned normally**. The executor's contract is `if (!result.ok)` → converge to `needs-human`, so a clean exit closed the work item **`outcome:done`**.

The specimen, from TLDR's own run last night:

| | |
|---|---|
| work item #268 | closed **`outcome:done`** at 00:14:23Z |
| PR #283 | open, labelled **`needs-human`**, "the converged tree FAILED its self-test" |

Same run, same moment. Every member's nightly update reported success like this for five days while the entire fleet sat frozen on one canon ref. The queue's signals were all green; nothing was.

The rehearsal path already exits non-zero on this exact terminal. Only the real path didn't.

## Why non-zero is right here

The house rule is "an expected, handled outcome exits clean; reserve non-zero for genuine breakage." A parked PR *is* the genuine breakage: the member has stopped converging, and nothing else in the system will say so. The label on the PR is not a signal anyone reads — five days of evidence.

## Verification

Seen to fail first: removing the `process.exitCode = 1` line fails the new test.

The test anchors on the terminal-dispatch block specifically, because the same `terminal.action === 'needs-human'` comparison appears twice earlier in the file on paths that already exit non-zero — anchoring naively passes against the wrong branch (which is exactly what my first draft did).

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1899 pass, 0 fail.**

## Live status

The unfreeze from #938 is confirmed working on a real member: TLDR's forced converge now returns terminal **`apply-stage`** (PR missingbulb/TLDR#290) instead of `needs-human`. Its self-test passes on the converged tree for the first time since 2026-08-12.

---
origin/main:engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-executor.yml:28:  actions: write
origin/main:engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-tick.yml:50:  actions: write         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (creating a workflow_dispatch event needs write; `read` silently 403s the POST)

# Claudinite work-item queue — the generator tick and its drain (tasks-dispatch
# DESIGN §5, §10). This is the repo's ONLY cron, and it replaces the slot
# scheduler's content at the same path when `taskScheduler.dispatch` is `"queue"`
# — same file, same hashed minute, different mechanism, so the one-cron rule and
# every reader that knows this workflow by name keep holding.
#
# A thin shim: all logic lives in the vendored engine, so this file changes
# rarely. The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap and the wiring converge
# rewrite it to this repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`.
#
# TWO JOBS, IN ORDER. The tick is pure label mechanics over the issue list —
# instantiate each task's standing item at its anchor, ready what is due, reclaim
# dead executor claims — and evaluates no precondition and collects no signal. The
# drain is an ordinary executor run: it picks up what the tick just created, which
# is what keeps the common case's latency at zero even with no `labeled` event
# delivered. Lost events are therefore never the only delivery — they are latency
# sugar, which is what retires the re-arm.
#
# `workflow_dispatch` is not a convenience: it is the never-wait-for-the-cron
# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on. Its one
# input is how that lever reaches ACROSS repos: the fleet enforcer dispatches
# this workflow naming the tasks to run now, and this member wakes its own
# standing items with its own token (DESIGN §8). The alternative — the enforcer
# editing every member's issues directly — would widen the fleet PAT to issue
# writes on every repository, for a job the member can do for itself.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '10 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wake:
        description: 'Task ids to run now (`pack/task` or a bare task name, space-separated) — wakes each one’s standing item regardless of its anchor'
        required: false
        type: string

# One tick at a time, always. The tick's duplicate-standing-item self-heal is
# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,
# which is safe precisely because two ticks never run at once.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-tick
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; a task's prework pushes its delivery branch
  issues: write          # create / label / comment / close work items — the queue itself
  pull-requests: write   # a task's prework opens its PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (creating a workflow_dispatch event needs write; `read` silently 403s the POST)

jobs:
  tick:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
